questions.q: Trade, which is a major division of commerce, is broadly categorized into two main branches known as
questions.explain: Trade is the exchange of goods and services for money. It is broadly divided into two major branches based on geographical boundaries: **home trade** (domestic) and **foreign trade** (international).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The buying and selling of goods and services within the geographical boundaries of a single country is referred to as
questions.explain: **Home trade**, also known as domestic or internal trade, involves transactions that occur strictly within the borders of a single country (e.g., selling goods from Kano to Lagos).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A businessman in Nigeria who buys electronic appliances from a manufacturer in Japan and sells them in his local market is engaging in
questions.explain: Because the transaction involves the crossing of international borders (buying from Japan and bringing into Nigeria), it is classified as **foreign trade**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Home trade is further subdivided into two distinct categories based on the volume of goods traded and the target buyer. These are
questions.explain: Within domestic borders, goods are distributed in stages. The two subdivisions of home trade are **wholesale** (buying in bulk) and **retail** (selling in small units).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The commercial process of buying goods in large quantities directly from the manufacturer and selling them in smaller batches to other traders is called
questions.explain: **Wholesaling** is the act of purchasing products in bulk (large quantities) from the producer/manufacturer and breaking the bulk to sell to retailers.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The trader who buys goods in small quantities from the wholesaler and sells them directly to the final consumer is known as a
questions.explain: A **retailer** sits at the end of the distribution channel. They purchase goods from wholesalers and sell them in single units or very small quantities directly to the people who will consume them.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Foreign trade is divided into two primary activities. What are they?
questions.explain: International or foreign trade consists of two main types: **Import** (bringing goods in from another country) and **Export** (selling local goods to another country).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Selling locally produced agricultural products like cocoa and cashew nuts to buyers in the United Kingdom is an example of
questions.explain: **Export trade** involves sending domestically produced goods to foreign countries for sale. Since the goods are going *out* of the local country, it is an export.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A major difference between home trade and foreign trade is that foreign trade usually involves
options: the use of different national currencies and exchange rates
only the use of physical cash without bank involvement
direct sales to final consumers in local markets
the total absence of transportation costs
questions.explain: Unlike home trade which relies entirely on the local currency, foreign trade crosses borders and therefore requires the **exchange of different national currencies** (e.g., converting Naira to Dollars or Yen).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following correctly pairs a major type of trade with its sub-divisions?
questions.explain: The correct structural classification is that **Home trade** is sub-divided into **Wholesale and Retail**. (Foreign trade is divided into Import and Export).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A trader who purchases $500$ bags of flour directly from a flour mill and resells them in batches of $10$ bags to neighborhood bakeries is operating primarily as a
questions.explain: This scenario perfectly describes a **wholesaler**, who performs the vital function of breaking bulk—buying heavily ($500$ bags) from the producer and distributing in smaller quantities ($10$ bags) to retailers/users.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All of the following activities are strictly categorized as divisions or types of trade EXCEPT
questions.explain: Wholesaling, retailing, importing, and exporting are all direct forms of *Trade*. **Insuring** (insurance) is an *Aid to trade*, meaning it facilitates the process but is not a form of trade itself.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Because foreign trade involves crossing international borders, it usually requires specific regulatory procedures such as
options: registering a local petty cash book
opening a savings account for children
questions.explain: International movement of goods is strictly regulated. Exporters and importers must undergo **customs and excise clearance** to ensure taxes are paid and contraband goods are not transported.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which trader in the channel of distribution usually provides the most direct and closest point of sale to the people living in a residential neighborhood?
questions.explain: The **retailer** (such as a local supermarket or kiosk owner) sets up shop near residential areas, making goods easily accessible to the final consumers.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In the standard distribution chain of home trade, who comes directly between the manufacturer and the retailer?
questions.explain: The traditional channel of distribution flows as follows: **Manufacturer $\rightarrow$ Wholesaler $\rightarrow$ Retailer $\rightarrow$ Consumer**. Therefore, the wholesaler acts as the middleman directly between the manufacturer and the retailer.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies
